Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is a slightly reworked mutual action plan that reflects the changes we discussed: tighter acceptance targets for the eval gate, and an explicit procurement milestone tied to your contract review. Key notes:

- Proposed new close anchor: target close 2026-11-30 (was 2026-11-10) — adds a 20-day buffer to accommodate procurement sign-off and SOC 2 evidence review.
- Eval checkpoints: three short, measurable evals (perf smoke, kv-cache stability, latency SLO verification) with owner and acceptance criteria on the MAP spreadsheet.
- Procurement step: we put a hard dependency on procurement sign-off (Procurement date) so downstream cutover doesn't start until that completes.

I attached the MAP (brighthealth_map_v1.xlsx) and a starter risk log (risk_log_20261023.csv) with initial items. Can you confirm that the revised anchor and checkpoints match BrightHealth's internal procurement window? If procurement needs more runway we can formalize a staggered go-live (phased acceptance) — happy to walk through options.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm procurement target (name and date) by EOD Friday 10/23.
2) Redwood to surface a recommended 30-day guarded buffer (exec ask) if procurement requires legal review beyond 10/27.
3) We schedule a short alignment call with Procurement and your Technical Reviewer early next week (15 minutes).

Thanks — I looped Jonas and Laura to ensure the MAP owners on our side are aligned.

Best,

Subject: Escalation: BrightHealth MAP slippage — exec ask

Team —

Short summary: BrightHealth's Legal has pushed procurement sign-off to ~2026-11-17. That creates a realistic risk to our previously-agreed close (2026-11-10) and requires an exec-level decision: either (A) accept a 30-day guarded buffer on the close anchor (recommended), or (B) approve a limited sandbox access and accept SLA credit exposure if cutover proceeds before full contract execution.

I've attached the initial risk_log_20261023.csv (rows below) and the MAP that shows revised milestones. Key risk items:
1) Procurement delay (Legal review) — likelihood: high; impact: high — blocks cutover and SLA start.
2) Data access gating — legal requires scoped data fields and audit hooks before engineering can run full evals.
3) Timeline compression — if we try to compress, support cost (Redwood engineering pre-seeding + prioritized trace) will increase and needs approval.

Suggested exec asks:
- Approve a 30-day guarded buffer to move Target Close to 2026-12-10 (exec sign-off to accept timeline risk and adjust revenue recognition cadence).
- Authorize a one-time credit reserve (up to $Xk, placeholder) for SLA ramp exposure if BrightHealth insists on rapid cutover prior to full contract execution.
- Approve an NDA addendum template for phased evals so we can enable technical checks earlier with minimal legal overhead.

Why recommended: a 30-day buffer preserves customer satisfaction during go-live, reduces risk of rushed cutover, and gives Redwood time to stage capacity changes if needed. The credit reserve is a standard commercial lever to close procurement concerns.

Action items from here:
- Jonas: cost estimate for prioritized engineering window and any incremental support GCs.
- Laura: commercial note (credit reserve wording + suggested cap) and draft of NDA addendum.
- Rachel: coordinate exec sync once Jonas + Laura have numbers (targeting end of day 10/25).

Elena / Marco — I copied you so there's transparency on our internal escalation. If BrightHealth prefers a different path, let us know and we'll adjust the MAP accordingly.
